text: Architecture documentation published in 2ab52e8. docs/adr/ holds seven accepted records in a fixed form (Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives considered) with an index: 0001 reference identity for extension keys, 0002 one typed error channel, 0003 separate scale training from encoding, 0004 resolve lengths once against one target, 0005 three compatibility courts, 0006 columnar marks stay one grob, 0007 provenance is a compiler policy -- the seven subjects the acceptance criteria name. docs/extending/ holds seven author guides (scales, stats, geoms, coords, recipes, backends, unsafe), each saying what you implement, giving a compiled example, and naming the law kit that proves it. Every example is fenced 'mdoc' and compiled against the real modules by tools/check-docs.sh, so the criterion 'compiled examples using only Intaglio's public API' is enforced rather than asserted. docs/extending/unsafe.md names the unsafe APIs and totality boundaries explicitly: every unsafe/orThrow entry point with what it throws and the total alternative beside it, plus the partial functions (DateScale#breaks, DatumIdSeries#valueAt, BatchColumn#valueAt, RegisteredScale#trained, DiscretePalette#apply, RasterImage.unsafeFromOwnedPackedArray) and the public case-class constructors carrying require, grouped by who touches them. Two findings are recorded there rather than silently fixed: Labeler has no checked twin, so a throwing labeler escapes ContinuousScale#labels; and Scale#trainPlotWide/trainFacet/observation are private[intaglio], so an ecosystem Scale cannot train and must declare ScaleTraining.Fixed. A fresh-context review of every new document against the sources found seven defects; all seven are fixed. One was a genuine overclaim in code rather than prose -- two guides said LineInterpolationLaws pinned the axis-transposition rule when it did not -- so the law was added to the kit instead of the claim being weakened. Not established: no documentation site is built or deployed; the records are read in the repository. ADRs are descriptive of decisions already implemented, not a design process.
